content: 1. For patients weighing ≤60 kg, administer didanosine extended-release 250 mg orally once daily or 125 mg orally every 12 hours. For patients weighing >60 kg, administer didanosine extended-release 400 mg orally once daily or 200 mg orally every 12 hours. Didanosine is indicated for the treatment of HIV infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents. 2. Didanosine should not be co-administered with the combination regimen of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, as this regimen is a complete treatment for HIV and does not require additional antiretroviral agents. 3. Febuxostat increases the levels and effects of didanosine by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Ribavirin increases the toxicity of didanosine through an unspecified mechanism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of hepatic failure, peripheral neuropathy, pancreatitis, and lactic acidosis. 5. Allopurinol increases didanosine levels through an unknown mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Patients should avoid taking antiretroviral therapies (ARTs) for at least one month before cell mobilization or until the medications are fully eliminated. 7. Didanosine decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin two hours before or six hours after didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution. 8. Hydroxyurea increases the toxicity of didanosine through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination should be avoided due to the risk of pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy, particularly in HIV patients. 9. Didanosine decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer levofloxacin two hours before or several hours after didanosine. 10. Didanosine decreases the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer moxifloxacin two hours before or several hours after didanosine. 11. Didanosine decreases the levels of ofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer ofloxacin two hours before or several hours after didanosine. 12. Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration of pexidartinib with other hepatotoxic agents, including didanosine. 13. Selinexor may cause neurological toxicities. Avoid combining selinexor with medications that increase the risk of dizziness or confusion. 14. Abacavir and didanosine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 15. Didanosine decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Administer atazanavir one hour before didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution. 16. Ritonavir decreases the levels of didanosine by increasing gastric pH. Didanosine should be taken one hour before or two hours after ritonavir or lopinavir/ritonavir oral solution. 17. Tenofovir DF increases the toxicity of didanosine by reducing its elimination. Use caution and monitor for signs of pancreatitis. 18. Methadone decreases the levels of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Didanosine decreases the levels of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. Administer itraconazole two hours before or several hours after didanosine. 20. Orlistat decreases the levels of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if virologic control is lost.
